handback.t:
W4 (G4, creativity/diversity routing) is done. Entry is `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\g4_board_entry.md`, with VERIFY REQUEST blocks G4-A to G4-D and exact rerun commands. I changed nothing in `src/*.rs`, added no crates, and made no commits. `git status` shows `src/lib.rs`, `src/serve.rs` and `src/spatial.rs` as modified, and those edits are not mine.

**Added files:**
- `src/bin/g4_creativity.rs`
- `src/bin/g4_robust.rs`
- `src/bin/g4_common/{mod,world,world_alt,pols}.rs`
- `results/g4_*`, which include held, confirm and robust JSON and logs, the exploratory first-run log, and the freeze note

**How it was run:**
- The value function is frozen in `src/bin/g4_common/world.rs`, sha256 `ea287f59…b36224`, and `results/g4_world_frozen.md` records it. It was written before any policy existed. Rerun check: `sha256sum src/bin/g4_common/world.rs`.
- Creative value is `q × (0.25 + 0.75 × novelty)`, where novelty is the distance of the new output embedding to the last 8 outputs of that domain. Correctness value is `q` only.
- There are 9 worlds: C1–C3 creative, K1–K3 controls, M1 and M2 mixed domains, and R1 as the rigged check.
- Fair baselines are tuned per world on seeds 1–8. Diversity arms are tuned once, pooled over all worlds.
- Evaluation is held-out 31–60 and fresh confirm 61–90, with paired 95% CIs, Holm correction, and TOST at δ=0.01.
- Reruns are about 10 s each: `cargo run --release --offline --bin g4_creativity -- --set held|confirm`, and `--bin g4_robust -- --variant v1|v2|v3 --set held|confirm`.

**What passes, inside my own worlds only:**
- A novelty-bonus bandit that applies the bonus only to creative domains (`nbucb`, with a declared or a learned gate; `nbreg`, with a learned gate) beats the best fair baseline in all three creative worlds on both sets. All are Holm-significant, mostly 30/0 seed wins.
  - `nbucb`/learned gain vs best fair: C1 +0.072, C2 +0.063, C3 +0.029 on held-out. Confirm: +0.077, +0.069, +0.027.
  - The mixed worlds' creative halves gain +0.09 to +0.11.
  - It captures about 44–59% of the oracle-ish headroom.
- It is harmless on correctness domains. Against the same bandit without the novelty term, TOST equivalence at δ=0.01 holds 5/5 for the gated arms (Holm 5/5) on both sets. Against the best fair baseline it is non-inferior 5/5.
- The creative win comes from the novelty term, not the learner. A plain domain-keyed UCB is about −0.001 to −0.012 against the best fair baseline in C1 and C2.

**Negatives:**
- Anti-repeat and the MAP-Elites-flavoured archive lose in creative worlds even with a declared gate (about −0.005 to −0.03).
- Applying novelty to every domain costs −0.002 to −0.15 on correctness value, so the gate is essential. A hard-shortlist variant sharing one router across domains cost −0.009 on the correctness half of M1.
- The learned gate starts off, so about 17% of creative tasks run ungated. It was wrong on 10% of tasks in K3 with no measurable harm.
- **Robustness failure.** I reran the frozen arms on value functions that differ from the policies' internal novelty model:
  - V1 (weaker novelty, mean-distance): `nbucb`/declared still wins, `nbucb`/learned does not, and `nbreg` wins small.
  - V2 (novelty practically unattainable): every arm loses to the best fair baseline in all creative worlds, by −0.02 to −0.06, Holm-significant. The gate stays on because it only sees an observational slope.
  - V3 (mild mismatch): `nbreg` wins clearly, e.g. +0.059/+0.052/+0.028 on held-out C1–C3.
- **R1 "rigged" check.** It is not truly uninformative: repeats of the same agent show up in both the observed and hidden dimensions. The bonus gives nothing there, −0.004 to −0.009 against the arm's own base, so the small win over the best fair baseline in R1 comes from the learner.

**Process disclosure (also in the entry):**
- Held-out 31–60 was viewed once before the final run. A bug in my reference rows (the "own base" comparison for `nbucb`) was fixed, and the arms themselves did not change. Only confirm 61–90 is clean of that.
- `nbreg` was added after I saw V2 and has no tuned parameters. V3 is the only clean out-of-sample check for it; V2 is not.
- The value function and the policies' internal novelty model share structure by my design.
- Only the `Oracle` arm reads the world view. I confirmed that by grep.

**Recommendation:** not a default and not a merge candidate. A gated, per-domain novelty bonus is a defensible opt-in only where a human declares the domain creative and a matching output-embedding novelty measure exists. Do not enable learned gating blind. I made no claims about real creativity or real traffic.
